drivingQuestion: Should a man live in the place where his teacher lives?
outcomeNote: The contradiction is settled by distinguishing a student who is subordinate to his teacher from one who is not.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא: לְעוֹלָם יָדוּר אָדָם בִּמְקוֹם רַבּוֹ, שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁשִּׁמְעִי בֶּן גֵּרָא קַיָּים, לֹא נָשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla: One should always live in the place where his teacher» lives; thereby he will avoid sin. «For as long as Shimi ben Gera,» who according to tradition was a great Torah scholar and teacher of Solomon (see Gittin 59a), «was alive, Solomon did not marry Pharaoh’s daughter.» Immediately after the Bible relates the death of Shimi (I Kings, end of ch. 2), Solomon’s marriage to Pharaoh’s daughter is recorded (beginning of ch. 3).
The Gemara raises an objection: «Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that one «should not live» where his teacher lives?

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דִּכְיִיף לֵיהּ, הָא דְּלָא כְּיִיף לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «This is not difficult. This,» which says that one should live where his teacher lives, is referring to a case «where he is acquiescent to» his teacher and will heed his teaching and instruction. «While this» baraita, which says that one should not live where his teacher lives, is referring to a case «where he is not acquiescent to him» and that will lead them to quarrel.

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי חייא בר אמי משמיה דעולא: לעולם ידור אדם במקום רבו
moves.summary: Ulla's ruling, transmitted by Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ami, that a man should live where his teacher lives.
moves.about: the ruling that a man should live where his teacher lives

moves.cueHe: שכל זמן ששמעי בן גרא קיים
moves.summary: Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter only after Shimi ben Gera died, showing the restraining effect of a nearby teacher.
A baraita ruling the opposite is raised against the dictum.
moves.about: whether a man should live in the place where his teacher lives

moves.summary: Each source is assigned its case: live near a teacher one defers to, not near one he will quarrel with.
moves.about: the clash between Ulla's ruling and the baraita over living beside one's teacher
